identity.trade: Cut stone: its quarry squared the stones of half the vale's waymarks, and its masons carve for the Guild at Silverford.

greeting: The shift bell is the only law in the pit. Mind it.
Stonehollow is quarry and masons. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Foremen are quitting. Not for money. For sleep.
A new shaft hit water and nobody could stop it. The water was warm.
A good waystone takes three weeks to cut and a day to crack, says the quarrymaster.

opinions.fulk_sedge: Fulk is good company and better at keeping quiet.
opinions.gerda_burrow: I would trust Gerda with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Welcome. Wipe your boots. Please. Soap is dear and floors are dearer.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
You look clean. Give it an hour.
rumour: Miners drink quick and tip slow. I water the first and ignore the second.
Somebody paid in old coin last night. Very old. Nobody knew the king on it.
The rock dust has a taste lately. Sweet, like iron and old pennies.
A cart of green-veined stone went north with a Runeward escort. Nobody says where.

opinions.colm_coalhill: Colm is good company and better at keeping quiet.
opinions.evelyn_thackeray: Evelyn has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Evelyn.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: Quick job or good job? I charge for both.
Strangers in Stonehollow get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Picks wear out in a week and wedges in a day. I keep a pile ready.
Hinges, hooks, wolf-bells. That is what sells now.
Pay day was delayed and nobody complained. When miners stop complaining, worry.

opinions.gerda_burrow: Gerda undercuts me. I forgive Gerda. Mostly.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: If it is not on the shelf, I can find it. If it cannot be found, I can find you something similar.
Folk come to Stonehollow for quarry and masons. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Candles, picks, tallow. Everything is bought by the dozen and burned by dusk.
Candles are short this month. The wax comes late, and so does the honest news.
A lamp flame leaned sideways in a sealed gallery. There is a draught from somewhere with no door.
Stonehollow lives by quarry and masons. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.colm_coalhill: Colm is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
The Stonehollow Quarry is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: I remember the Long Dark. Nobody asks. Nobody wants the answer.
The ore carts run late. The road is fine. The carters are afraid.
The deep quarry face hums at night. The masons have stopped working past dusk.

opinions.leofric_rawlin: Leofric lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: Stone does not care how your morning went.
You will hear Stonehollow before you see it. Ask at the Stonehollow Quarry.
rumour: The old cut has a step in it. Too neat for a quarryman, too wide for a mason. We do not go there.
Pit props are failing on the third level. The foreman says rot. The crew says a knock.

opinions.aubrey_harker: Aubrey works hard and talks harder.
opinions.reda_birkett: Reda keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: Mind the order of things, friend. There. Now we can talk.

greeting: Stone is patient. I am less so.
Lamp up and mind the timber. We say it twice and mean it.
rumour: The old waymark at the ford is cracked. Not worn. Struck.
The mine cat will not go below the second level. He is the best judge of air we have.

opinions.bettany_hornby: Bettany works hard and talks harder.
opinions.leofric_rawlin: Leofric keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

greeting: Good ore rings. Bad ore thuds. Everything else is lies.
Dust is the town's second weather. Mind your lungs.
rumour: Seams are thinner. The carts are still full of waste.
The pit ponies shy at the same turning every shift. The foreman has stopped using that turning.
The Stonehollow Quarry was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.leofric_rawlin: Leofric knows the trade. I will say that for Leofric.

time.rain: Rain. The pit floods and the pumps groan. Everybody bails.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever. I would say a pun-ctual friend, but you heard it last time.

greeting: Steel does not wait for talkers. State your business.
Stonehollow is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: The furnace burned blue yesterday. Nothing I fed it burns blue.
Strange scratches on the tunnel wall, above head height. We stopped the dig.

opinions.una_netherby: Una works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Look what the wind dragged in. Sit. Do not touch the pie.

greeting: Road is long, axle is short.
Welcome to Stonehollow. Mind the Stonehollow Quarry. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Toll at the ford has gone up. So has my temper.
The deepest miner swears the rock breathes. He is not drunk, which is the worrying part.
If trade slows, Stonehollow feels it first. If it speeds up, Stonehollow feels it last.

opinions.bettany_hornby: Bettany knows the trade. I will say that for Bettany.
opinions.uther_chandler: Uther works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: Walk with me? I cannot stay still, and you are good company on the move.

greeting: My back says no. My purse says yes.
First time in Stonehollow? The Stonehollow Quarry is the place to start.
rumour: Someone is hiring after dark. I did not ask for whom.
When Stonehollow is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.leofric_rawlin: Leofric works hard and talks harder.
opinions.sidony_elder: Sidony knows the trade. I will say that for Sidony.

greeting: Mind the lamp. Mind the roof. Mind me.
rumour: A tunnel we closed in spring was open this morning. Nobody dug it.
The Stonehollow Quarry has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.sander_keld: Sander works hard and talks harder.
opinions.sorrel_hornby: Sorrel and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

greeting: Lamp up, helmet down. We talk later.
rumour: The north shaft is shut again. The foreman says the roof. The miners say not.
Ask anyone in Stonehollow about the Stonehollow Quarry. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.bettany_hornby: Bettany works hard and talks harder.
opinions.esmer_hatch: Esmer knows the trade. I will say that for Esmer.

time.morning: Shift is up. Bring a lamp, bring a prayer.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: Coal dust never leaves. Not the lungs, not the stew.
rumour: The roof sang at dawn, a low note. Everyone stopped. Then everyone went back to work.
Whatever you hear about Stonehollow, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.esmer_hatch: Esmer works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Shift is done. Wash the dust off, if the water allows.

dialogue.aside: A friend is a rare coin. I have spent worse.

greeting: Mind the lamp. Mind the roof. Mind me.
rumour: Something knocks back when you knock on the deep face.
A stranger asked at the Stonehollow Quarry for the oldest person in Stonehollow. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.elfrida_fletcher: Elfrida works hard and talks harder.
opinions.uther_chandler: Uther knows the trade. I will say that for Uther.

time.night: Night shift. Keep your voice low. The rock listens.

dialogue.aside: My friend. Come, I kept something for you. A small thing. It means a lot to me.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: I saw a light in the hedge last night. Do not tell Mum.
The mine cat will not go below the second level. He is the best judge of air we have.

opinions.bettany_hornby: Bettany and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A survey stone sits a hand's width from its mark. The old socket is clean.
A pit prop charred at the foot. Someone lit a small fire and stamped it out.
A chain cut clean with a good tool and wrapped to look whole.
Prints too big for a dog, heading for the tree line.
A dragged carcass. Teeth marks, not knife marks.
A rail splintered outward, wool snagged on the edge.

stashes.say: You drag four trimmed blocks onto the barrow.
